problem_summary.summary: Choose two vertical lines that, with the x-axis, enclose the greatest possible area.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: heights of n vertical lines at consecutive horizontal positions. Return the maximum area min(height[i], height[j]) * (j - i).

brute_force.explanation: Evaluate every pair of line indices and retain the greatest area they form.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every container is defined by one pair i < j. The nested loops visit all such pairs and compute each pair's limiting height times its width, so the largest stored value is the answer.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only scalar values are stored.

optimized.explanation: Begin with the widest pair. After measuring its area, move the pointer at the shorter line inward; moving the taller side cannot improve the limiting height and only reduces width.
optimized.correctness_idea: For a fixed shorter boundary, every inward pair that keeps that boundary has strictly less width and no greater limiting height, so it cannot beat the measured area. Discarding the shorter boundary therefore cannot discard a better pair; repeating this argument considers an optimal pair before the pointers meet.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) — each pointer moves inward at most n times in total.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary — only pointers and the best area are stored.

steps.event: Measure the outer lines at indices 0 and 3.

steps.action: Keep best at 10 and advance left; the pointers meet.

edge_cases.handling: The initial pair is the only possible container.

edge_cases.case: One or both lines have height zero
edge_cases.handling: Their computed area is zero and the scan continues to test other pairs.
The implementation advances the left pointer; either shorter-side choice is safe when heights tie.
